EN:
I went to the Dryad island and found an Elven settlement. The priestess told me that the Elves are tolerated on the island because they are repelling the repeated invasions from the Wastelands with their ships. She also said that the Queen’s decision is not really popular among the Dryads. Many of them think that the Elves are destroying the island by farming, mining and cutting down the trees.
I have been away from the island for too long, so according to our laws I'm now considered a foreigner until I regain the trust of my family. The priestess gave me a task to prove my loyalty. I must shut down the strip mine west of here, because it's polluting the air by constantly belching clouds of smoke into the sky.
PTBR:
Fui à ilha das Dríades e achei um povoamento Élfico. A Sacerdotisa me contou que os Elfos são tolerados na ilha porque estão repelindo as invasões repetidas dos Ermos com os navios deles. Ela também disse que a decisão da Rainha não é bem popular entre as Dríades. Muitas delas acham que os Elfos estão destruindo a ilha lavrando, minerando e cortando as árvores.
Estive fora da ilha por tempo demais, então, conforme as nossas leis, agora sou considerada estrangeira até readquirir a confiança da minha família. A Sacerdotisa me deu uma tarefa para provar a minha lealdade. Tenho que desligar a mina a céu aberto a oeste daqui, porque ela está poluindo o ar, eructando nuvens de fumaça constantes no céu.

From one warrior to another, I bequest you locate the Lost Lorebook of Atherton, and to deliver its message to a trusted Chronicler. He will know what to do. Tragam a glória de volta à família Real Atherton!

EN:
Protect me from these thugs!

The moneylender has deceived me. I wanted to sew dresses to sell at the market. He sold me cloth for 100 gold, on credit of course. But the cloth was moth-eaten, not even fit for potato sacks. Now his thugs are threatening me and demand his money back. Please protect me!

EN: Welcome to Badawi, my friend! I am Pasha Barazi and I run the local arena. You picked a good day to come here because we just got some new merchandise and are testing it in battle today. That's just your thing, isn't it? You look like you're well traveled and like you have enough experience to be able to show a couple of greenhorns some new tricks. Since we don't have another selector, you could take care of it for me. Just go into the arena and test out our newbies!
PTBR: Bem-vindas a Badawi, minha amiga! Eu sou o Paxá Barazi e administro a arena local. Vocês escolheram um dia bom para vir aqui, porque acabamos de receber mercadoria nova e estamos testando ela em batalha hoje. Isto é justamente a sua praia, não é? Vocês parecem bem viajadas e com experiência o bastante para mostrar umas novas pegadinhas a uns casais de novatas. Como não temos outra seletora, vocês poderiam dar conta disto por mim. Só entrem na arena e testem as nossas novatas!

EN:
Get back the lost pieces of wrought-iron work!

You look like you might be able to help me. You must know that our blacksmith is a true expert, and has finally taken me on as his apprentice. This really means a lot to me. And now, on my first important mission, this happens to me! He wanted me to go to the capital to get some things that he needed for a job. On my way back, I was robbed by a malicious gang of thieves and robbers! I was able to escape, but without my master's things.

You should find them in a small cave south of the city. Please help me. I'll be waiting for you at the blacksmith's place.
PTBR:
Recuperem as peças perdidas de ferraria!

Vocês parecem que poderiam me ajudar. Vocês devem saber que o nosso ferreiro é um verdadeiro especialista, e finalmente me aceitou como aprendiz dele. Isto significa bem muito para mim. E agora, na minha primeira missão importante, isto me acontece! Ele queria que eu fosse à capital buscar umas coisas que ele precisava para um trabalho. No caminho de volta, fui assaltada por uma gangue malvada de ladrões e assaltantes! Consegui escapar, mas sem as coisas do meu mestre.

Vocês deveriam achá-las numa pequena caverna ao sul da cidade. Por favor, ajudem-me. Estarei esperando por vocês no lugar do ferreiro.

EN: I’m really happy that you made this decision! My brothers thought you’d be much more patient. That’s a topic we’ve been arguing about for years now. Os meus irmãos achavam que poderiam ocupá-la com todo tipo de tarefas diferentes por toda a eternidade, mas você provou que eles estavam errados: então eu venci a aposta. EN: Although these Humans are free, they are socially disadvantaged. They make ends meet by working for little pay, or begging. Most of them have no formal education. PTBR: Embora estes Humanos sejam livres, eles são socialmente desfavorecidos. Eles se viram trabalhando por pagamento baixo ou mendigando. A maioria deles não tem instrução formal nenhuma. EN:
In order to reach the key, you must get past the Facetteleon

Welcome back to the home of your ancestors, sister. You have been away for a long time. Forgive me for not revealing myself earlier; I needed to get to back to the safety of my sanctuary as quickly as possible. This abduction was no coincidence. The Inquisitors wanted to force me to reveal the location of the key to them, and but for you they would have succeeded!
I owe you my life. Your name shall never be forgotten amongst our kind, for you will be known as she who saved Dyria D´Arquelyght, Archon of the Dryads!
So you are looking for the key as well? Alas, I have bad tidings for you. The key rests in the safest possible place, the Crystal Cavern to the north, which is guarded by a fearsome monster, the Facetteleon. I fear that your quest is futile. No one has succeeded in overcoming this guardian.
PTBR:
Para alcançar a chave, vocês têm que passar pelo Facetteleon

Bem-vinda de volta ao lar das antepassadas de você, irmã. Você esteve fora por muito tempo. Perdoe-me por não me revelar antes; eu precisava voltar à segurança do meu santuário o mais rápido possível. Este sequestro não foi coincidência nenhuma. As Inquisidoras queriam forçar-me a revelar a elas a localização da chave, e, se não fosse por você, elas teriam conseguido!
Eu vos devo a vida. O seu nome jamais será esquecido entre as do tipo de nós, pois você será conhecida como ela que salvou Dyria D'Arquelyght, Arconte das Dríades!
Então você também está buscando a chave? Ai de mim: tenho más notícias para você. A chave repousa no lugar mais seguro possível, a Caverna de Cristal ao norte, que é guardada por um monstro temível, o Facetteleon. Temo que a sua busca é fútil. Ninguém teve sucesso em superar este guardião.

EN:
Destroy the Dryad's strike force and bring me seven of their heads!

Enough is enough! Those Dryads keep trying to strong arm us! As if that wasn't enough, they're making shrunken heads from our fallen comrades! Just imagine seeing your best friend's head dangling from a Dryad witch's belt. This is hurting our morale!
I have a plan! We're just going to turn the tables on them! Yes sir! We're going to make shrunken heads out of them. Our scouts have spotted a strike force of Dryads near here. Slaughter them and bring me their heads! We're going to teach them a lesson!
PTBR:
Destruam a força de ataque das Dríades e tragam-me sete das cabeças delas!

Basta! Aquelas Dríades continuam tentando usar força bruta conosco! Como se não bastasse, elas estão fazendo cabeças reduzidas dos nossos companheiros caídos! Só imaginem ver a cabeça da melhor amiga de você balançando no cinto de uma bruxa Dríade. Isto está machucando a nossa moral!
Tenho um plano! Vamos simplesmente inverter a mesa contra elas! Sim, senhor! Vamos fazer cabeças reduzidas delas. As nossas batedoras avistaram uma força de ataque de Dríades perto daqui. Espanquem elas e tragam-me as cabeças delas! Vamos ensinar uma lição a elas!

EN:
A Revolutionary Idea

-But what's it good for?
-Good for, good for. Why does everything always have to be good for something? Besides: have you never asked yourself how that would be?
-Hmm .. don't know. Maybe sometimes. But never for long. I guess ... you can't turn a blind eye on reality.
-That's not what this is about. And anyway...
Poldina, the beautiful waitress put two full tankards on the table between Milan and Golros and put the empty ones on her tray without saying a word. Ignoring them, she turned on her heel and went over to the bar.
 -... and anyway: look at us! I. Dropped out of the Mages' Academy, got two illegitimate kids to pay for. Now I am earning my living with the writing of short manifestos and speeches for the high-and-mighty council members whose brains are too small or too lazy to produce a thought worthy of the paper it's written on. And what about you? A small-time crook who can barely survive on what he makes with semi-legal odd jobs. And if you don't hit the jackpot during one of your burglaries and find the damned dragon's treasure in a golden chest soon, nothing will change for you either. That's fact! Is it really so surprising to try and ignore it, even for a little while?
-Nah, 'course not. But you should stay realistic. Let's take my aunt Hannahfee for example ... they nicked her ...
-Nicked her?
-Yeah ... took her. Nicked her. Locked her away. 'Cause she thought she was Seraphim Sophia herself and started preachin' on the market place.
-And they nicked her for that? There's always one preacher or another on the market place.
-She preached to the chickens in the cages and called them “winged sisters”.
-Oh ... I see. But that's something completely different. Your aunt wasn't cognizant. She couldn't help herself. But us ... we are free. What I'm saying is: we're not bonkers!
-Aunt Hannahfee didn't go bonkers! She's just got ... an alternative perception of reality.
-Whatever. The result remains the same. They wanted to nick her either way. The point is: she didn't have a choice! We do. It's like a dream, only you're not sleeping.
-Fine. One imagines one's someone else. What then? And what's so special 'bout it?
-Simply this: You tell the others.
-Huh? The others? Which others?
-Well, the others who also imagine they are someone else.
-I'm tellin' others I'm not the one I am, but I'm someone else? And they tell me the same? Forget it! No way! That'd be embarrassin'.
-How do you know it's embarrassing? You haven't tried it, yet.
-I do know what's embarrassin' and what's not, thank you.
-But if everyone is doing it, it can't be embarrassing anymore, right? And besides ...
The waitress strode past Milan and Golros with a full tray and put it down on the table next to theirs. While she blew a lock of hair from her face, which had loosened from her bun, she put the tankards on the large table. When she turned, she glanced at the two men's tankards. Golros looked at her, and their eyes met for just a moment. He spontaneously and unsuccessfully tried an easy smile when Poldina turned around and disappeared in the direction of the bar. Golros' eyes followed her - his face still frozen in a strained smile.
 -Golros?
-Huh?
-... and besides: it's a lot of fun!
-But why others? If I want to imagine bein' someone else, I don't have to tell others 'bout it! I can do it all for meself.
-That's not the same! If it's all only in your head, everything will happen the way you want it to happen! There are no surprises, nothing unforeseen.
-I thought that was the idea ...
-No! The idea is that different people react in different ways. You won't know what will happen. Everything else would be unrealistic.
-'Bout as unrealistic as imaginin' to be someone else.
Milan sighed but decided not to give up so quickly and try once more.
 -What about when you were young? Did you never play Warriors and Orcs when you were a kid? With wooden swords and all that?
-Sure did!
-See! You weren't embarrassed then, were you?
-Kids are never embarrassed. Kids don't know what embarrassed means. Discoverin' embarrassment happens when you grow up.
-But you had fun whacking the evil orc with your wooden sword as a kid, right?
Golros stared at his tankard in silence.
 -RIGHT?
-Yeah ... sure!
-Well! What would you like to be? What did you want to be when you were a kid?
Golros considered the question for a while.
 -A supermage throwin' lightnin'. With robe and staff. Who fries everythin' in his way!
Milan nodded appreciatively.
- I would like to be a barbarian warrior. You know, one of those with a two-handed double axe who ... BAM ... hacks his enemies in pieces before they know what hit them.
-Not bad! We'd be a good team, the two of us. You at the front, me in the background throwin' lightnin' and fire.
Milan imagined how a lightning-throwing mage and a raging barbarian fought against a legion of orcs.
 -The orcs wouldn't even touch us!
-And afterwards, we could loot 'em. Orcs'll surely have lots of gold, arcane magical artifacts and healin' potions.
-And we would share the loot fairly of course. Just like brothers in arms do!
-Right ... fairly and under consideration of the performance. Two third for me, the rest for you.
-Oh, and why is that? My ax would have killed at least as many orcs as your stupid lightning bolts, if not more!
-Don't be ridiculous! A supermage is a deadly weapon. You can't kill enough orcs to keep up with him.
-You wouldn't stand a chance against me.
-Bah! You'd have a fireball in your face before you could raise your ax!
-Before you’d be done with your mumbo jumbo, your brain halves would only be able to communicate via long distance signal!
Golros and Milan looked at each other in silence.
 -Hm ... looks like imagination alone is not enough. Someone should invent a way to determine the winner of such battles.
-If you think we’re going to the woods now to fight it out ... you with a wooden ax and I throwin' grain sacks ... you're barkin' up the wrong tree. We could go an' join aunt Hannafee right here and now.
-No, no ... nothing like that. Something different. Maybe tossing a coin. Or ... or we could simply toss dice.
-Toss dice! It's really becomin' more ridiculous by the minute. You say we're sittin' around a table, thinkin' we're someone else and if one doesn't like what's what, we're tossing dice to see who's right?!
-Oh well ... all right. I admit, it would be a bit strange. But there must be something we could do. I'll think about it some more.
PTBR:
Uma Ideia Revolucionária

-Mas para que ela serve?
-Servir, servir. Por que tudo tem sempre que servir para algo? Além disso: você nunca se perguntou como seria?
-Hmm .. não sei. Talvez às vezes. Mas nunca por muito tempo. Acho ... que a gente não pode fechar os olhos para a realidade.
-Não é disto que se trata. E de qualquer forma...
Poldina, a linda garçonete, pôs duas canecas cheias na mesa entre Milan e Golros e pôs as vazias na bandeja dela sem dizer uma palavra. Ignorando elas, ela virou nos calcanhares e foi para o balcão.
 -... e de qualquer forma: olhem para nós! Eu. Desisti da Academia dos Magos, tenho dois filhos ilegítimos para sustentar. Agora ganho a vida escrevendo manifestos curtos e discursos para os membros poderosíssimos do conselho, cujos cérebros são pequenos demais ou preguiçosos demais para produzir um pensamento digno do papel em que é escrito. E você? Um estelionatário de pequeno porte que mal sobrevive do que ganha com biscates semi-legais. E se você não acertar a loteria num dos seus arrombamentos e achar o tesouro maldito do dragão num baú dourado em breve, nada mudará para você também. Isto é fato! É mesmo tão surpreendente tentar ignorá-la, mesmo que por um pouquinho?
-Nem, claro que não. Mas você devia ficar realista. Vamos pegar a minha tia Hannahfee como exemplo ... eles afanaram ela ...
-Afanaram ela?
-É ... levaram ela. Afanaram ela. Trancaram ela. Porque ela achava que ela era a própria Serafim Sophia e começou a pregar na praça de mercado.
-E eles a afanaram por isto? Sempre tem um pregador ou outro na praça de mercado.
-Ela pregava para as galinhas nas gaiolas e as chamava de "irmãs aladas".
-Oh ... entendi. Mas isto é completamente diferente. A sua tia não era lúcida. Ela não se controlava. Mas nós ... nós somos livres. O que digo é: nós não somos malucos!
-A tia Hannahfee não ficou maluca! Ela só tem ... uma percepção alternativa da realidade.
-Tanto faz. O resultado permanece o mesmo. Eles queriam afanar ela de qualquer jeito. O ponto é: ela não tinha escolha! Nós temos. É como um sonho, só que você não está dormindo.
-Certo. A gente imagina ser outra pessoa. E aí? E o que é tão especial nisso?
-Simplesmente isto: Você conta para os outros.
-Hã? Os outros? Quais outros?
-Pois: os outros que também imaginam ser outra pessoa.
-Eu conto para os outros que eu não sou quem sou, mas sou outra pessoa? E eles me contam o mesmo? Esquece! De jeito nenhum! Isto seria embaraçoso.
-Como você sabe que é embaraçoso? Você ainda nem tentou.
-Eu sei o que é embaraçoso e o que não é, obrigado.
-Mas se todo mundo faz, não pode mais ser embaraçoso, certo? E além disso ...
A garçonete passou por Milan e Golros com uma bandeja cheia e a pôs na mesa ao lado da deles. Enquanto soprava, para longe do rosto, um cacho de cabelo que tinha se soltado do coque, ela pôs as canecas na mesa grande. Quando ela se virou, deu uma olhada nas canecas dos dois homens. Golros a olhou, e os olhos deles se encontraram por só um momento. Ele tentou espontaneamente e sem sucesso um sorriso fácil quando Poldina se virou e sumiu na direção do balcão. Os olhos de Golros a seguiram: a face dele ainda congelada num sorriso forçado.
 -Golros?
-Hã?
-... e além disso: é muito divertido!
-Mas por que os outros? Se eu quero imaginar ser outra pessoa, não preciso contar para os outros! Posso fazer tudo por mim mesmo.
-Não é a mesma coisa! Se é tudo só na sua cabeça, tudo vai acontecer do jeito que você quer que aconteça! Não há surpresas, nada imprevisto.
-Eu pensava que era esta a ideia ...
-Não! A ideia é que pessoas diferentes reagem de jeitos diferentes. Você não vai saber o que vai acontecer. Tudo o resto seria irrealista.
-Tão irrealista quanto imaginar ser outra pessoa.
Milan suspirou mas decidiu não desistir tão rápido e tentar mais uma vez.
 -Que tal quando você era jovem? Você nunca brincou de Guerreiros e Orcs quando era criança? Com espadas de madeira e tudo isto?
-Brinquei sim!
-Viu! Você não ficava embaraçado então, ficava?

A Revolutionary Idea

-But what's it good for?
-Good for, good for. Why does everything always have to be good for something? Besides: have you never asked yourself how that would be?
-Hmm .. don't know. Maybe sometimes. But never for long. I guess ... you can't turn a blind eye on reality.
-That's not what this is about. And anyway...

 -... and anyway: look at us! I. Dropped out of the Mages' Academy, got two illegitimate kids to pay for. Now I am earning my living with the writing of short manifestos and speeches for the high-and-mighty council members whose brains are too small or too lazy to produce a thought worthy of the paper it's written on. And if you don't hit the jackpot during one of your burglaries and find the damned dragon's treasure in a golden chest soon, nothing will change for you either. That's fact! Is it really so surprising to try and ignore it, even for a little while?
-Nah, 'course not. But you should stay realistic. Let's take my aunt Hannahfee for example ... they nicked her ...
-Nicked her?
-Yeah ... took her. Nicked her. Locked her away. 'Cause she thought she was Seraphim Sophia herself and started preachin' on the market place.
-And they nicked her for that? There's always one preacher or another on the market place.
-She preached to the chickens in the cages and called them “winged sisters”.
-Oh ... I see. But that's something completely different. Your aunt wasn't cognizant. She couldn't help herself. But us ... we are free. What I'm saying is: we're not bonkers!
-Aunt Hannahfee didn't go bonkers! She's just got ... an alternative perception of reality.
-Whatever. The result remains the same. They wanted to nick her either way. The point is: she didn't have a choice! We do. It's like a dream, only you're not sleeping.
-Fine. One imagines one's someone else. What then? And what's so special 'bout it?
-Simply this: You tell the others.
-Huh? The others? Which others?
-Well, the others who also imagine they are someone else.
-I'm tellin' others I'm not the one I am, but I'm someone else? And they tell me the same? Forget it! No way! That'd be embarrassin'.
-How do you know it's embarrassing? You haven't tried it, yet.
-I do know what's embarrassin' and what's not, thank you.
-But if everyone is doing it, it can't be embarrassing anymore, right? And besides ...
The waitress strode past Milan and Golros with a full tray and put it down on the table next to theirs. While she blew a lock of hair from her face, which had loosened from her bun, she put the tankards on the large table. When she turned, she glanced at the two men's tankards. Golros looked at her, and their eyes met for just a moment. He spontaneously and unsuccessfully tried an easy smile when Poldina turned around and disappeared in the direction of the bar. Golros' eyes followed her - his face still frozen in a strained smile.
 -Golros?
-Huh?
-... and besides: it's a lot of fun!
-But why others? If I want to imagine bein' someone else, I don't have to tell others 'bout it! I can do it all for meself.
-That's not the same! If it's all only in your head, everything will happen the way you want it to happen! There are no surprises, nothing unforeseen.
-I thought that was the idea ...
-No! The idea is that different people react in different ways. You won't know what will happen. Everything else would be unrealistic.
-'Bout as unrealistic as imaginin' to be someone else.
Milan sighed but decided not to give up so quickly and try once more.
 -What about when you were young? Did you never play Warriors and Orcs when you were a kid? With wooden swords and all that?
-Sure did!
-See! You weren't embarrassed then, were you?
-Kids are never embarrassed. Kids don't know what embarrassed means. Discoverin' embarrassment happens when you grow up.
-But you had fun whacking the evil orc with your wooden sword as a kid, right?
Golros stared at his tankard in silence.
 -RIGHT?
-Yeah ... sure!
-Well! What would you like to be? What did you want to be when you were a kid?
Golros considered the question for a while.
 -A supermage throwin' lightnin'. With robe and staff. Who fries everythin' in his way!
Milan nodded appreciatively.
- I would like to be a barbarian warrior. You know, one of those with a two-handed double axe who ... BAM ... hacks his enemies in pieces before they know what hit them.
-Not bad! We'd be a good team, the two of us. You at the front, me in the background throwin' lightnin' and fire.
Milan imagined how a lightning-throwing mage and a raging barbarian fought against a legion of orcs.
 -The orcs wouldn't even touch us!
-And afterwards, we could loot 'em. Orcs'll surely have lots of gold, arcane magical artifacts and healin' potions.
-And we would share the loot fairly of course. Just like brothers in arms do!
-Right ... fairly and under consideration of the performance. Two third for me, the rest for you.
-Oh, and why is that? My ax would have killed at least as many orcs as your stupid lightning bolts, if not more!
-Don't be ridiculous! A supermage is a deadly weapon. You can't kill enough orcs to keep up with him.
-You wouldn't stand a chance against me.
-Bah! You'd have a fireball in your face before you could raise your ax!
-Before you’d be done with your mumbo jumbo, your brain halves would only be able to communicate via long distance signal!
Golros and Milan looked at each other in silence.
 -Hm ... looks like imagination alone is not enough. Someone should invent a way to determine the winner of such battles.
-If you think we’re going to the woods now to fight it out ... you with a wooden ax and I throwin' grain sacks ... you're barkin' up the wrong tree. We could go an' join aunt Hannafee right here and now.
-No, no ... nothing like that. Something different. Maybe tossing a coin. Or ... or we could simply toss dice.
-Toss dice! It's really becomin' more ridiculous by the minute. You say we're sittin' around a table, thinkin' we're someone else and if one doesn't like what's what, we're tossing dice to see who's right?!
-Oh well ... all right. I admit, it would be a bit strange. But there must be something we could do. I'll think about it some more.
